terra.problem: Established sovereignty and royal power do not establish that the kingdom was steady or that things were going well.
“Nobody signed anything” asserts more than the passage says about a treaty.
The drawer joke suggests Papa found his own way out. An angel took him out, so the joke misrepresents his backstory.
“One after another” adds a sequence the text does not give for the capture of the cities.
The passage says Shishak came as far as Jerusalem, not that his army was right outside the city when Shemaiah spoke.
The haggling joke has no connection to an action in the passage. No one tries to bargain with Shemaiah.
The text does not say that the king and leaders offered no arguments or excuses, or that the army was parked outside.
The passage records their humility and words, but does not say they offered no defense or speech.
“They stood there” adds a posture the text does not give.
Papa says he hid in the drawer, but he was put there. It is also a second drawer joke in the same stop, after card 4, answer 3.
“No complaining, no pointing fingers” asserts behavior the passage does not describe.
The passage does not say the army was still outside when the LORD spoke to Shemaiah.
The promise that wrath would not be poured out through Shishak does not establish that no part of Jerusalem burned.
“The people aren't being sent anywhere” asserts more than the passage says.
The dull-edged stamper comparison clashes with Papa's backstory: his worn edges produced blurry stamps, and he was replaced.
The text says the shields were returned to the guardroom, not to a shelf.
“Daily routine” adds a frequency. The text says the guards carried the shields whenever the king entered, not that he entered every day.
The explanation is generic and repeats the same point without much of Papa's voice.
The passage describes an attack, but does not say Jerusalem was besieged.
“Right after he humbled himself and things went well” suggests a timing the passage does not give for its assessment of Rehoboam.
“Never set itself” goes beyond the text's statement that he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.
The explanation is generic and largely repeats the quoted answer without Papa's distinctive voice.
“No peace treaty, no friendly neighbors” adds details the passage does not give. “Just war for as long as they both lived” also makes the stated war throughout their days sound continuously ongoing.
Jeroboam's identity as king of Israel needs a reference outside this passage.
“The fighting with him never ended” turns war throughout their days into a claim of uninterrupted fighting.
Jeroboam's identity as king of Israel needs a reference outside this passage.
The statement that Rehoboam had other sons needs a reference outside this passage, such as 2 Chronicles 11:18–20.
